title: Singular partitive with i → e
summary: For this group of words, change final i to e before adding -a/-ä: ovi (“door”) → ovea, nimi (“name”) → nimeä. Keep strong consonants, as in lehti (“newspaper”) → lehteä. Other -i words follow different patterns.
objectives: Form the singular partitive in this bounded word family.

sections.title: Meaning and pattern
paragraphs: A case is a word form used for a grammatical job. The dictionary form is the form used to look up a word. The partitive has several uses; it does not always mean “some”. Here you practise forming the word, so no sentence construction is required.
These particular i-ending words change their last i to e before -a/-ä. Keep their strong consonant stem. Membership of this family is learned word by word; many other i-words retain i.
keyPoints: Learn each word with its pattern; a similar final letter does not guarantee the same stem.

steps: Change final i in ovi to e, keep the strong consonants, and add -a: ovea.
The word’s meaning stays connected to “door”; its singular case form changes its grammatical use.
Change final i in nimi to e, keep the strong consonants, and add -ä: nimeä.
The word’s meaning stays connected to “name”; its singular case form changes its grammatical use.
Change final i in järvi to e, keep the strong consonants, and add -ä: järveä.
The word’s meaning stays connected to “lake”; its singular case form changes its grammatical use.
Change final i in lehti to e, keep the strong consonants, and add -ä: lehteä.
The word’s meaning stays connected to “newspaper”; its singular case form changes its grammatical use.
Change final i in mäki to e, keep the strong consonants, and add -ä: mäkeä.
The word’s meaning stays connected to “hill”; its singular case form changes its grammatical use.
Change final i in joki to e, keep the strong consonants, and add -a: jokea.
The word’s meaning stays connected to “river”; its singular case form changes its grammatical use.
Change final i in kivi to e, keep the strong consonants, and add -ä: kiveä.
The word’s meaning stays connected to “stone”; its singular case form changes its grammatical use.
Change final i in suomi to e, keep the strong consonants, and add -a: suomea.
The word’s meaning stays connected to “Finnish language”; its singular case form changes its grammatical use.

commonMistakes: Do not treat every i-ending word as this family.
Keep strong k in mäkeä and j in jokea.
The language name suomi is written with a lower-case initial.
